instructions: Look at the following film reviews and the statements following them.
Your task is to match the statements 1-9 to reviews A-D.
body: A) City Lights (1931)
Starring: Charlie Chaplin, Virginia Cherrill
Director: Charlie Chaplin

One of Charlie Chaplin's best films - and his last silent film. This film is a classic black and white silent masterpiece (with sound effects). In the city, the tramp (Chaplin) falls in love with a blind flower-selling girl (Cherrill), and although he is poor, she thinks he is a millionaire. Her sight is restored thanks to his efforts.
Academy Awards: 1, Best Director.
B) Snow White And The Seven Dwarfs (1937)
Starring: Voices of Harry Stockwell, Lucille La Verne, Adriana Caselotti
Director: David Hand, Perce Pearce

Disney's first full-length, commercially-successful animated masterpiece, a classic, adapted Brothers Grimm fairy tale with a vain, evil Wicked Queen (La Verne), the Queen's beautiful step-daughter Snow White (Caselotti), seven gold-mining dwarfs who whistle to and from work at the diamond mines - and a Prince Charming.
Recipient of Special Award.
C) 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968)
Starring: Keir Dullea, Gary Lockwood, HAL 9000
Director: Stanley Kubrick

Kubrick's metaphoric, thought-provoking, grandiose, science-fiction landmark film, with space travel to Jupiter, the appearance of mysterious stone monuments, and the presence of the film's major character - a super-computer. A team of robotic-like astronauts Bowman (Dullea) and Poole (Lockwood), during a voyage to Jupiter are terrorized by the arrogant, humanistic, on-board computer HAL 9000. The mission fails, and Bowman is reborn within a divine embryo that floats in space.
Academy Awards: 1, Best Special Visual
D) Some Like It Hot (1959)
Starring: Marilyn Monroe, Tony Curtis, Jack Lemmon,
Director: Billy Wilder

Wilder's funny comedy. Two unemployed Chicago jazz musicians, Joe (Curtis) and Jerry (Lemmon) accidentally witness a crime, and must flee from gangsters. They pretend to be women and join Sweet Sue's all-girl band with singer Sugar Kowalczyk (Monroe) heading for Florida to escape. With the greatest closing line in film history: "Nobody's perfect."
Academy Awards: 1, Best B/W Costume Design.

body: Cycling has become popular over the past few years. Below you can read some top tips on how to get on your bike.
BUYING A BIKE

Your first port of call should be a good bike shop. There are thousands nationwide, all {{0}}. Don’t just go to the one closest to you; visit a few. Ask as many questions as you need to about which sort of bike would suit you best.
When you’ve found a good shop, ask the shop for advice on buying the correct size for you. Autumn is an ideal time to buy a bike as manufacturers bring out their new models, {{10}}.
Mountain bikes If you live in a rural area and will occasionally be going off road, a mountain bike is the best bet. Many have suspension and offer thicker tyres, {{11}}.

Road bikes The advantage of these is that you can pull up the pedals as well as push down on them, which can be as much as 10% more efficient, as well as {{12}}. Road bikes have enjoyed a renaissance recently, thanks to the popularity of the Tour de France and other races.
Hybrid bikes These are excellent for riding in traffic. Hybrid bikes can take pannier racks, which are useful for {{13}}.
Folding bikes Using folding bikes can mean {{14}}: you might drive to the train station, carry your bike onto the train and then cycle from the train station to your destination at the other end.
Just 30 minutes exercise a day could quite literally be a lifesaver, as well as {{15}}.
It can also save travel costs and, of course, help a safer and cleaner environment.

body: Opera fans watch for dark skies Belfast opera fans will be watching the skies this week as they prepare for a night of outdoor virtual opera.
Botanic Gardens in Belfast is hosting a live broadcast of La Boheme on Thursday night, from London's Royal Opera House.
The tragic tale of the love of a sick working girl for a poet in 18th century Paris is the third time Opera in the Park has come to the city.
Last year rain caused a lot of problems and with rain forecast again organisers are urging people to dress appropriately.
The council said the free performance, which is also shown simultaneously in a number of English cities, is a chance to see the rising stars of opera in action.
Gates open at 17.00, with entertainment on the Great Lawn from 17.15, featuring the Irish Three Tenors.
The main performance, broadcast from Covent Garden, starts at 21.30.
